messages.author: 84d40346d2b44e80
messages.subject: Windows clipboard
parts:
Hi All,

I created a plot using Plot Builder and now want to copy the result
from the JavaGD window to Word. The usual combination of CTRL-C, CTRL-
V just copies as a low-res image. Saving to PDF and EPS are high-res
formats, but Word will not display them. Word will display a TIFF, but
it's just a bit mapped version of my plot. I can use ggsave to write a
wmf file which displays in Word in high resolution, but people drawn
to Deducer are not likely to be thrilled with a code-and-file based
alternative to a simple cut/paste. This is a trivial thing to do in
RGUI. What am I missing?

Thanks,
Bob

Hi Bob,

I have found using ggplot2 (and via Deducer) that the PNG format is
always the best for MS Word docs.

I is easily pasted in that much crisper that JPG files.

Bruce

messages.author: 267c7c6c510dc8a2
messages.subject: Re: Windows clipboard
parts:
Bob,

As Bruce said you can save the plot as png. Word also does allow you
to import a pdf plot (just drag it from the file system onto your
document). However, I think that the effect that your seeing may be
due to copying an image that is small. Try resizing the plot to make
it bigger, and then copy and pasting it.


Ian

messages.author: 84d40346d2b44e80
messages.subject: Re: Windows clipboard
parts:
Ian & Bruce,

Thanks very much for the help. I was sure I was missing something really fundamental since this works in RGUI so well. I thought I'd runs run Plot Builder from RGUI but apparently the graphs have nowhere to go without JGR. 

The PDF did indeed display in Word when I gave it more space, but it was a PDF of a low-res bitmap! When I used png, it was a much higher-res bitmap and it looked good. If it had been a Windows metafile, I could have edited it, changing fonts, etc. but everything has its limitations. Deducer is fantastic software. I hope the ability to cut and paste will get added to JGR eventually making it more like a standard Windows program. 

Does the Mac version have high-res cut/paste ability?

Thanks,
Bob
